 CLARITY Act LIVE Updates Today September 15: The CLARITY Act is winning the spotlight in Washington today. It is gaining momentum as the U.S. Senate set to vote on a critical measure that will be essential to the advancement of the crypto market structure legislation that’s been long awaited. As the bill moves a crucial step in the legislative process, lawmakers are under increasing pressure to agree on a bipartisan compromise.
 The Senate’s cloture vote is under the radar of the crypto industry, investors and market participants, due to the gravity of its possible impact on the digital asset regulation in the United States. The passage would be a major milestone but it was not a sure sign of passage. Stay up to date with the most recent developments for the CLARITY Act, along with lawmakers’ remarks and market responses in our live updates.

 CLARITY Act LIVE Updates Today September 15: The CLARITY Act is winning the spotlight in Washington today. It is gaining momentum as the U.S. Senate set to vote on a critical measure that will be essential to the advancement of the crypto market structure legislation that’s been long awaited. As the bill moves a crucial step in the legislative process, lawmakers are under increasing pressure to agree on a bipartisan compromise.
 The Senate’s cloture vote is under the radar of the crypto industry, investors and market participants, due to the gravity of its possible impact on the digital asset regulation in the United States. The passage would be a major milestone but it was not a sure sign of passage. Stay up to date with the most recent developments for the CLARITY Act, along with lawmakers’ remarks and market responses in our live updates.
-->
 07:15:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 Breaking: Democrats Who Backed CLARITY Act Talks Vote NO, Delivering Major Blow
 Key Democrats who were working on the CLARITY Act in the past few months have voted ‘No’ on the cloture motion, journalist Eleanor Terrett reported. Those lawmakers include Sens. Kirsten Gillibrand, Mark Warner, Cory Booker, Raphael Warnock, Ruben Gallego, Angela Alsobrooks and Catherine Cortez Masto. The ballots were received “despite negotiations” with the legislation, Terrett said.
 🚨NEW: Several Democrats who have spent months negotiating the Clarity Act, including Gillibrand, Warner, Booker, Warnock, Gallego, Alsobrooks and Cortez Masto, have all voted NO.
 One industry leader just texted me: “It died.” https://t.co/L3phIIWNsK 
 — Eleanor Terrett (@EleanorTerrett) September 15, 2026 
 “One industry leader just texted me: ‘It died,’” she wrote. Failing to invoke cloture is a serious setback for the crypto market structure bill.
 Share this update:
 06:40:00 PM UTC, 16 September 2026
 Breaking: CLARITY Act Fails To Move Forward In US Senate Cloture Vote
 The CLARITY Act has failed to secure the 60 votes needed to advance in the U.S. Senate, with the unofficial tally at 46 Yes to 43 No. However, some senators are still left to vote but the final outcome has not yet been determined as already 43 Senators have voted against it.
 The vote is an important one for the digital asset market structure bill following a disagreement between Republicans and Democrats over changes to the bill, especially ethics clauses. But the negotiations continued until the last minute, with Democrats insisting on more revisions to the bill.
 Share this update:
 06:25:00 PM UTC, 16 September 2026
 Breaking: US Senate CLARITY Act Cloture Vote Today!
 The U.S. Senate has started to vote on a motion to invoke cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 3633, the Clarity Act, which would introduce a bill to the crypto market structure. Republicans and Democrats continue to have a fight over ethics provisions and other proposed changes.
 NOW VOTING: Motion to invoke cloture on the motion to proceed to Cal. #423, H.R.3633, Clarity Act.
 — Senate Cloakroom (@SenateCloakroom) September 15, 2026 
 This cloture motion needs 60 votes from the 100 senators. Negotiations have been going on until the bitter end, and there are still more changes in the works from the Democrats. Even though the election is close, the Clarity Act is given just 20% chance of passage in 2026.
 Share this update:
 06:15:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 Warren: Trump’s Crypto Fortune Surpassed Every Publicly Traded U.S. Crypto Company
 Ahead the CLARITY Act cloture vote, Sen. Elizabeth Warren took aim at President Donald Trump’s crypto ventures during a speech in Congress. She said he “opened his own crypto business” shortly before being sworn in for a second term.
 Warren described the launch as “what a launch that man had,” claiming that as Trump “talked up crypto,” the “money just kept rolling in.”
 She said Trump and his family “raked in $1.4 billion” from crypto ventures in 2025. Warren added that Trump “made more from crypto last year” than any publicly traded crypto company in America.
 Share this update:
 06:05:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 Just 10 Minutes Left: Clarity Act Vote Hangs By A Thread as Ethics Talks Go Down
 With just minutes until senators vote on the Clarity Act, negotiations on Capitol Hill remain tense as lawmakers race to reach a deal. Democrats still want changes to bill’s ethics provisions and any more tweaks may need another White House stamp.
 With just an hour to go until senators vote on the Clarity Act, the mood among negotiators on Capitol Hill is tense as talks come down to the wire. 
 Democrats are still holding the line on changes to the bill’s ethics provisions. Any further tweaks would likely require another… https://t.co/dc4wmfO1Ql pic.twitter.com/DCd9fHNBDe 
 — Eleanor Terrett (@EleanorTerrett) September 15, 2026 
 “Lots of really hard work is going on. But time is very short,” a Democratic source said. A Republican source said they shared the same concern. But anything can happen in Congress, according to an industry source that says the bill will face just a 60 vote hurdle to pass.
 Share this update:
 04:45:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 Leaked Docs Reveal Senate Democrats Proposing Stricter Ethics Rules
 In their latest counterproposal on digital assets, Senate Democrats want to impose stricter ethics rules and apply them to the relatives of federal officials. The change is somewhat more sweeping, expanding the scope beyond just officials to include their families in the restrictions to cryptocurrency transactions.
 The proposal also increases standards for those who hold major digital-asset interests, such as mandates for divesting or setting up a so-called blind trust. The ethics framework would be ramped up for certain large holdings, with the trustees required to divest within 180 days.
 Share this update:
 04:15:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 Sen. Cynthia Lummis Warns Clarity Act Could Be "Over" if Cloture Vote Fails
 Senator Cynthia Lummis warned today that if the cloture motion to consider the Clarity Act was denied, negotiations could come to a close. Speaking to reporters, Lummis said, “I think we’re done. It’s over. Because we’ve been working on this bill for over a year, and we’ve given them over 120 of their requests. That’s enough.”
 Sen. Cynthia Lummis (R-Wyo.) tells a large gaggle of reporters that if the Clarity cloture vote fails today, "I think we're done. It's over. Because we've been working on this bill for over a year, and we've given them over 120 of their requests. That's enough."
 — Brendan Pedersen (@BrendanPedersen) September 15, 2026 
 The alert comes as Republicans and Democrats are embroiled in a bitter wrangle over the bill’s provisions. The Senate must have at least 60 votes for cloture, so today’s vote is pivotal for the bill’s future.
 Share this update:
 03:30:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 Breaking: Thom Tillis Says Confirms 'Yes' Vote In Favor of Clarity Act Cloture
 Senator Thom Tillis, who has remained silent in the previous days, confirmed this morning that he will vote to move forward with cloture on the Clarity Act as Senate negotiations heat up. Tillis expressed his “very pleased with the ethics provisions that the White House put together.”
 Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) says this morning he’s going to vote for cloture on the Clarity Act, saying he’s “very pleased” with what the White House delivered on ethics. 
 “If it doesn't address their concerns, once it's amendable, then don't vote for it on the back end”
 — Brendan Pedersen (@BrendanPedersen) September 15, 2026 
 His remarks come on the heels of President Donald Trump’s recent agreement to the measures. He also said in a statement that he would give the senators an opportunity again to reject the bill if their concerns are not resolved. “If it doesn’t address their concerns, once it’s amendable, then don’t vote for it on the back end,” Tillis said. He indicated that he was for passage of the bill but maintained a conditional approval.
 Share this update:
 03:15:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 White House Crypto Adviser Questions Banking Lobby’s Clarity Act Opposition
 Washington’s banking lobby is opposing the CLARITY Act. However, White House crypto adviser Patrick Witt says he’s not sure if its fears about deposit flight are reflected in its actions. On X, Witt said that banks should be “aggressively whipping Senators, both Republican and Democrat, to get on the bill” if they’re truly interested in the protection that they’ve been asking for.
 If the DC banking lobby were serious about their deposit flight argument, they would be aggressively whipping Senators, both Republican and Democrat, to get on the bill and then push for changes after. Because if this bill fails, they get none of the protections they claim to…
 — Patrick Witt (@patrickjwitt) September 15, 2026 
 The industry can push for changes after, he added. “Because if this bill fails, they get none of the protections they claim to desperately need,” Witt wrote. He further added, “They haven’t done that. Draw your own conclusions.”
 Share this update:
 03:00:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 French Hill Stays Optimistic As Senate Prepares For Crucial CLARITY Act Vote
 French Hill, Chairman of the House Financial Services Committee, said that he is hopeful that today’s Senate vote on the CLARITY Act is likely to result in a bipartisan deal. Hill cited in an interview with CNBC’s Squawk Box that the months of work included Sens’. Tim Scott, Cynthia Lummis and others.
 🚨 BREAKING: 🇺🇸 House Financial Services Chair French Hill says he’s optimistic about today’s CLARITY Act vote.
 Speaking to @CNBC ’s Squawk Box, Hill expressed confidence as the Senate takes up the bill.
 All eyes are on the Senate today. pic.twitter.com/LMge0eqx8u 
 — Conor Kenny (@conorfkenny) September 15, 2026 
 “I’m optimistic,” Hill said in referring to a proposal that Democrats are now considering. Hill said he would be happy to establish “a framework for digital assets” through legislation rather than leaving regulation solely to agencies. He also emphasized the need for permanent rules, which “can’t be reversed” by the future chair of the SEC or the CFTC.
 Share this update:
 02:40:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong Presses Senators Ahead of Clarity Act Vote
 Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong has been appealing to lawmakers to pass the CLARITY Act , as they prepare for a crucial vote today. Armstrong said the decision is between the U.S. taking the lead in innovation of crypto or letting other countries do it.
 Senators pick one of two choices today:
 1. vote yes on the CLARITY Act to promote innovation, protect consumers, put new ethics restrictions on elected officials, and create new law enforcement tools to combat illicit finance, or 
2. vote no and let other countries lead in… https://t.co/VYautgxf1S 
 — Brian Armstrong (@brian_armstrong) September 15, 2026 
 “Senators pick one of two choices today,” he wrote on X. He said a yes vote would “promote innovation, protect consumers” and introduce new ethics restrictions and law enforcement tools. Armstrong warned that a no vote could let “other countries lead in building the future of finance.” “History—and the crypto voter—won’t forget.”
 Share this update:
 02:30:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 Sen. Warner Spox Fires Back as Clarity Act Debacle Heats Up Ahead of Cloture Vote
 A spokesperson for Sen. Mark Warner responded to Republican objections about the latest Clarity Act demands by the Democrats as tensions escalate leading up to today’s cloture vote. The spokesperson said the provisions reflect “language Democrats have been seeking for the better part of a year.”
 A spokesperson for Tim Scott pans Democrats’ latest crypto counter:
 “In response to a significant step in their direction, Democrats have chosen to move the goalposts again.
 “Republicans made 126 substantive changes at Democrats’ request, including major changes to address…
 — Eleanor Mueller (@Eleanor_Mueller) September 15, 2026 
 They said that the measures are “commonsense safeguards” that must be put in place to ensure consumers, national security, market integrity, ethics and law enforcement are protected. The battle comes as neither side wants to back down with 60 votes required to move forward with the law.  “Addressing these priorities is essential,” Warner’s spokesperson said, to building a durable U.S. crypto market.
 Share this update:
 02:20:00 PM UTC, 14 September 2026
 Tim Scott Slams Democrats Crypto Counter-Offer, Urges Support For Clarity Act Vote
 A spokesperson for Senate Banking Chairman Tim Scott criticized Democrats’ latest counter-offer in negotiations over the Clarity Act, accusing them of repeatedly shifting their demands. The spokesperson said Republicans had made “126 substantive changes at Democrats’ request,” including major revisions addressing ethics concerns.
 A spokesperson for Tim Scott pans Democrats’ latest crypto counter:
 “In response to a significant step in their direction, Democrats have chosen to move the goalposts again.
 “Republicans made 126 substantive changes at Democrats’ request, including major changes to address…
 — Eleanor Mueller (@Eleanor_Mueller) September 15, 2026 
 “Yet we are hearing the same unreasonable asks and the same refusal to take yes for an answer,” they added. Further, they noted that the final text reflects more than a year of bipartisan negotiations. Republicans urged Democrats to “stop playing games” and support to advance the Clarity Act.
 Share this update:
 01:50:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 Republicans Reject Democrats Clarity Act Counter-Offer: Lummis Spox Says No Progress
 Democrats have offered a counter-offer in ongoing negotiations over the Clarity Act, but Senate Republicans have rejected it, indicating that there are significant differences between the two sides. Sen. Cynthia Lummis (R-Wyo.)’s spokesperson, Katie Warbinton, said that Democrats “have not budged an inch.” In a letter to congressional leadership, Warbinton contended that the new offer is mostly a repetition of the Democrats’ earlier demands, and not one that would provide any new compromises.
 NEWS 🚨: Republicans dismissed a Clarity Act counter-offer from Democrats. Spox for Lummis (R-Wyo.) says Democrats "have not budged an inch."
 "They need to actually start negotiating instead of resubmitting the same demands and calling it progress." https://t.co/2SQMZi8fhN pic.twitter.com/rubXCOSES5 
 — Brendan Pedersen (@BrendanPedersen) September 15, 2026 
 “They need to actually start negotiating instead of resubmitting the same demands and calling it progress,” she said. There were also new changes and restrictions to crypto ethics in the Democratic proposal, along with modifications to protections for DeFi and tribal gaming. Read More. 
 Share this update:
 01:30:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 CLARITY Act 2026 Approval Odds Drop To 20% As Senate Clash Deepens
 The odds of the CLARITY Act passing in 2026 have plummeted since the newest version of the act, as Senate Republicans and Democrats continue to debate the final wording of the bill. The odds of passage this year are now at 20%, lower than a day ago’s 34%, signifying a weakening outlook.
 According to data from Kalshi, the chances of the bill becoming law are 20% before January 1, 2027. But as for the prospects of approval before October 1, it is only 6%. The drop is significant as lawmakers continue to hold talks before the Senate’s critical cloture vote.
 Share this update:
 01:15:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 White House Pushes Stablecoin Data Tool Ahead of CLARITY Act Senate Vote
 The White House is stepping up its campaign to garner support in the Senate from Republicans for the CLARITY Act, and banking issues regarding stablecoins are one of the sticking points. Authorities are working on an interactive website that will enable users to explore scenarios on the development of stablecoins and bank deposits. The platform will also answer to the criticism directed at the earlier report submitted by the Council of Economic Advisers and answer some of the most frequently raised questions.
 News: The White House is going all out to convince Senate Republicans to advance landmark crypto legislation today over banks’ concerns.
 Officials plan to launch an interactive tool that allows users “to set the parameters, run the scenarios, and see for themselves” why CEA… pic.twitter.com/vARnage5En 
 — Eleanor Mueller (@Eleanor_Mueller) September 15, 2026 
 White House crypto advisor Patrick Witt defended the administration’s findings as he said, “The data simply does not support the deposit flight narrative that DC bank lobbyists are pushing.” The push follows as lawmakers are mulling the crypto bill before a vote on it is made today.
 Share this update:
 12:55:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 Senate Democrats Prepare Counteroffer Hours Before CLARITY Act Vote
 Democrats have introduced an alternative plan for the CLARITY Act, adding another layer of confusion to the Senate’s cloture vote. The Democratic lawmakers engaged in negotiations are offering up their own plan, Sen. Mark Warner said. He stated, “The Democrats who’ve been working on this in good faith are sending a counterproposal.”
 A new version with stricter ethics provisions that were aimed at President Donald Trump had been circulated among Republicans recently. Democrats, however, had complained that the measures were not designed to deal with possible conflicts of interest. Sen. Raphael Warnock said, “I don’t think Democrats should advance a bill that doesn’t deal with these opportunities for corruption we’re seeing in real time,” per PunchBowl news report. Read More. 
 Share this update:
 12:30:00 PM UTC, 15 September 2026
 Coinbase CEO Armstrong Bullish On CLARITY Act Clearing 60-Vote Senate Hurdle
 Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong recently expressed a strong bullish narrative that the CLARITY Act will clear the Senate’s 60-vote cloture vote requirement. He said, “I’m pretty optimistic that we’re going to get more than 60 votes.” The cloture vote would allow the bill to advance to debate but would not mean final passage.
 CLARITY ACT: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong says, "I'm pretty optimistic that we're going to get more than 60 votes ."
 Armstrong says thousands of hours of bipartisan work have gone into the bill, moment” for U.S. crypto and finance. 🤝 pic.twitter.com/MUTLZDSQmx 
 — Orange Man Vlad (@orangmanviad) September 15, 2026 
 Further, Coinbase Chief Policy Officer Faryar Shirzad also outlined the expected timeline. He noted, “There will be a series of votes…over maybe 10 days. If we get passed the first vote we feel pretty good about that we’re on pretty much a glide path to get to the end state.” Read More.
